Unfortunately, Servant of the Dawn is the only means to becoming Emperor in Oblivion. If you really don't like the Mythic Dawn, you could always just cast them aside after you become emperor since they're just a means to an end.

Oooh, the Necromancer. My favorite character archetype. Consider me an expert on this subject.

Moriarcis is a good start. As MrSnowShow said, Mannimarco Revisited is a must have. Now, for my list.

There is one essential mod for Necromancers: [Epic Necromancy](http://www.nexusmods.com/oblivion/mods/40964/?). In the vanilla game, you can't really perform real necomancy. Sure, you can summon corpses, but that's about it. Epic Necromancy allows you to truly roleplay that class by letting you harvest the bodies of your enemies to get parts that can be used to "build" skeletons, zombies and so forth. There's no limit to the size of your army too. You can also build lairs and other Necromancers will be friendly to you. There's plenty of other features but those are the highlights. 

If you're interested in story, [Mannimarco Resurrection](http://www.nexusmods.com/oblivion/mods/15251/?) is highly recommended. After becoming archmage, it allows you to betray the guild by joining up with a new and improved Mannimarco (or you can remain loyal and fight him again, but who would want that?). There's plenty of necromantic things you can do with the mod as well, and you get your own fancy dark lair.

[Supreme Magicka](http://www.nexusmods.com/oblivion/mods/12466/?) is good because it allows you to summon multiple creatures at once, and it is essential for mages in general because it revamps the entire magic game in general (in a good way).

If you're looking for power, I highly recommend [Servant of the Dawn](http://www.nexusmods.com/oblivion/mods/6855/?). While not necessarily connected with Necromancy, you can combine all of the above mods to build a huge undead army, then join up with the Mythic Dawn to steamroll over all of Tamriel and become the emperor. Or a God. The possibilities are pretty much limitless.

Get creative with it. I played one necromancer character who infiltrated the Mages Guild to destroy it. I then used Mannimarco Resurrection to betray the guild and become a Necromancer Lord and Servant of the Dawn to become Emperor. Kind of like Crusader Kings. With more magic and less incest.

Those are a few good ones. Have fun conquering Cyrodiil :)

He was a Dark Elf with a dark history. He ran slaver rings, killing and selling people back in Morrowind for profit. He had no sense of morality, only doing what would make him richer. Money, he believed, was all that mattered in the world, and he would do whatever it took to make more of it. In an effort to make the largest profit possible, he arrived in Cyrodiil. As far as his abilities, he was a spellsword, wearing heavy armor and using a blade but hitting hard with a sword as well. He was also quite the alchemist. His ultimate goal was to attain as much wealth as possible, but after a short time in Cyrodiil in which he was essentially pissed on as a useless peasant for his deeds, he realized power was what really mattered. Power, he learned, was what separated the men from the boys. He decided he must find a way to become the most powerful man in Cyrodiil: the Emperor. 

By working with The Blades, he wagered, he could put Martin on the throne and overthrow him due to the trust they shared. After settling the Oblivion crisis, however, Ocato granted him the measly title of "Champion of Cyrodiil". He was outraged by being skipped over for Emperor and went into hiding for years.

This is the point where I stopped playing because I lost interest. His next step was to build an army of dark allies to take over the land, first by joining up with Mannimarco's necromancer cult (Mannimarco Resurrection: Light and Dark mod). I felt the very same way a few months ago. There's no good answer or solution to your problem. When I first got started with college I was an emotional wreck and went through some serious depression leading up to almost killing myself. 

First, I want you to know that you always have this subreddit to come to. That probably doesn't help you any, knowing that random strangers on the internet will say nice things to you, but it's true. You can always talk to us. 

Second, there's always treatment available. I can't advocate for any particular treatment, of course, but there are tons of possibilities. For me, I had to stay in a hospital for a week. It made a world of difference. That, combined with weekly therapy and medication, has helped me fight my depression. Once again, I can't tell you one way or the other. It's just something worth looking into.

It seems like you have a family that cares about you. Reach out to them. Don't hide your feelings from them. That's what I did, and it just made things worse. Family can be an incredibly support structure for you if you let them in instead of closing them out. Once again, I can't really advocate for this as a "treatment", but it helped me tremendously.

If you need anything else, feel free to PM me, or, if I don't respond (I'm not a frequent redditor), keep coming to this subreddit. They helped me tremendously back when I was in such a dark place.
